steps.body: If the tens make 10 or more, trade 10 tens for 1 hundred.
steps.narration: If the tens make 10 or more, trade 10 tens for 1 hundred.

widget.prompt: Build 340 with no more than 9 blocks in each place. Trade 10 rods for 1 flat.

commonBuilds.feedback: Fourteen rods do not fit in one place. Trade 10 of them for 1 flat.

widget.missFeedback: That build names a different number — total each unit's worth and match 340 exactly.
widget.successFeedback: 3 flats and 4 rods — the fourteen tens traded ten of themselves into a flat.

predict.prompt: 6 tens + 8 tens: what do ten of those tens become?
predict.reveal: Ten tens are exactly one hundred — the bundle moves into the hundreds place.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2b trade tens.
invariants: Trading between places changes the form of a quantity, never its value — the model and the number must stay equal for g2b trade tens.
misconceptions: Treating a trade as adding or removing amount instead of renaming the same total.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the blocks stop matching the written number?

commonErrors.feedback: The ten tens you bundled never became a hundred — carry it into the hundreds place.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Line the places up — hundreds with hundreds, tens with tens, ones with ones — and work one column at a time.

widget.prompt: A build shows 11 tens. What does trading do with them?

options.label: Trade ten of the tens for one hundred
options.feedback: Correct — ten tens and one hundred are the same amount, so trading changes the form, never the value.

options.label: Throw away the extra tens
options.feedback: Discarding tens shrinks the number; a trade must keep the total exactly equal.

options.label: Turn each ten into a hundred
options.feedback: One ten is worth ten, not a hundred; only a GROUP of ten tens equals one hundred.

options.label: Leave 11 tens — numbers cannot hold that many
options.feedback: Eleven tens are allowed, but trading 10 tens makes the number easier to read.
